# Mérida The cultural, academic, and economic metropolis of southeastern Mexico. Centered around a dense, historic colonial grid and rapidly expanding outward along concentric ring roads and radial avenues, Mérida challenges transit planners to unite sprawling suburban bedroom communities, booming financial and commercial corridors, a vast ecosystem of higher education campuses, and the northern coastal port of Progreso into a seamless, high-capacity regional network. ## Coverage

## Additional Features - **Concentric Urban LOD Architecture** — Advanced Level-of-Detail filtering concentrates residential streets, minor roads, and 3D buildings within the high-density urban core footprint, while retaining key highways, expressways, and coastal horizons across the broad regional BBOX. - **Ocean & Gulf Bathymetry** — Features custom bathymetric elevation depth-coloring across the Gulf of Mexico, coastal ports, and coastal lagoons near Progreso. - **Higher Education Special Demand** — Models 23 dedicated university campuses with specialized student-commuter damping algorithms (0.3) reflecting real-world off-peak trip distributions. - **Dedicated Airport POI** — Integrated regional air passenger node for Mérida International Airport (MID). ## Demographics & Calibration Demographic and employment distribution is calibrated using microdata from the Mexican National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI) 2020 Population and Housing Census (`RESAGEBURB`) down to individual urban blocks (*manzanas*), synchronized with official CONAPO municipal demographic projections for 2026. Zero centroid imputation is applied outside delineated urban polygons. Commercial mass, employment nodes, and service clusters are integrated from the contemporary National Directory of Economic Units (DENUE) with 6-digit SCIAN classification and calibrated against municipal Censos Económicos (CE) macro-totals. Commuting trips are synthesized using a double-constrained Furness entropy gravity model with strict mass conservation ($\sum T_{ij} \equiv \sum \text{PEA}_i$), while vehicular travel baselines follow canonical free-flow routing (~40 km/h) calculated via Open Source Routing Machine (OSRM). ## Reference Sources - **INEGI:** Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020 (CPV - Microdatos por Manzana Urbana `RESAGEBURB`) - **INEGI:** Directorio Estadístico Nacional de Unidades Económicas (DENUE 2024–2026) - **INEGI:** Censos Económicos (CE) y Encuesta Nacional de Ocupación y Empleo (ENOE Yucatán) - **CONAPO:** Proyecciones de la Población de los Municipios de México 2020–2070 - **OpenStreetMap & Geofabrik:** Road geometry, 3D building outlines, and natural waterways - **ASUR:** Mérida International Airport (MID) passenger throughput statistics ## License Open Database License (ODbL) for underlying OpenStreetMap data; INEGI & CONAPO open data terms of use. ## Credits - **Map Author:** Meszier83 - **Cartographic Data:** © [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/) contributors, [Geofabrik GmbH](https://download.geofabrik.de/). - **Demographic & Statistical Modeling:** Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía ([INEGI](https://www.inegi.org.mx/)) & Consejo Nacional de Población ([CONAPO](https://www.gob.mx/conapo)). - **Routing Engine:** Open Source Routing Machine ([OSRM](http://project-osrm.org/)).
